newsitem.title: INDIA: Chidambaram expects India's 97/98 budget on time.
newsitem.headline: Chidambaram expects India's 97/98 budget on time.

text.p: Finance Minister P. Chidambaram expects to present India's 1997/98 (April-March) budget on time at the end of February, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said on Tuesday.

Officials said Chidambaram's remarks could help ease recent speculation in the Indian media that the ruling United Front alliance may have problems presenting the budget because of growing difference with the Congress party.
Prime Minister H. D. Deve Gowda's alliance is surviving with make-or-break support from the Congress in parliament.
Chidambaram made his remark to reporters after launching the Finance Ministry's home page on the Internet information highway on Tuesday.
Some newspapers have said Deve Gowda might consider dissolving the Lok Sabha and order snap polls after presenting an interim budget, if the Congress presses on with its campaign against him.
PTI quoted Chidambaram as saying he also expects a review of the controversial corporate Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT), opposed by industry.
However, it said Chidambaram would review the MAT only when two draft financial laws he proposes to move in parliament are in place by January.
"Once the Companies Act and Income Tax Act are more closely aligned, the cause for MAT may disappear," PTI quoted a senior finance ministry official as saying.
Chidmabaram hopes that the debate on the two bills will commence in January.
